samples.summary: Login callback server again redeems the first `code` that hits the loopback port, with no binding to the flow this process started
samples.evidence: This delta reverts the nonce/`state` echo end to end: `startCallbackServer()` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:153-182) now resolves `callbackPromise` for any `GET /callback?code=…` with no check that the code belongs to this login, `github-auth.guard.ts:24` no longer stores a nonce, and `auth.controller.ts:127` no longer echoes one back. The CLI then exchanges that code at `/auth/cli/exchange` and `saveSession()` (login.ts:138) persists whatever account it maps to, overwriting the user's session. The port is guessable and any page in the user's browser can navigate to it (RFC 8252 §8.9), so the terminal can be silently pointed at another account's session. The deleted `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` was the only regression guard. Primary ownership is the security lens; raised here because the outcome is a wrong/overwritten persisted session (state corruption), and because the delta also removes the only test of that behaviour.

samples.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` can pair a nested `error.code` with an unrelated top-level `message`
samples.evidence: The fallback chain `messageText(fields.message) ?? messageText(body?.message) ?? messageText(raw)` reads the top-level `message` even when the body already carries a structured `{ error: { code, … } }` object that simply lacks a `message`. In that case the emitted envelope mixes sources: `code` comes from the nested error object while `message` comes from an unrelated top-level field (e.g. Nest's generic `"Bad Request"`), producing a code/message pair that never existed on the server. Preferring the top-level text only when no nested `error` object is present would avoid the mismatch.

samples.summary: `messageText` silently drops non-string elements of a `message` array
samples.evidence: `messageText` filters an array down to non-empty strings and joins them; if Nest's ValidationPipe (or a custom filter) puts constraint *objects* in `message`, every element is filtered out, `parts.length === 0`, and the function returns `undefined`, so the server's text is dropped and the envelope falls back to `HTTP <status>` — the very flattening this change set out to avoid. Mixed arrays lose the object entries with no indication.

finding.summary: Login callback server again redeems the first `code` that hits the loopback port, with no binding to the flow this process started
finding.evidence: This delta reverts the nonce/`state` echo end to end: `startCallbackServer()` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:153-182) now resolves `callbackPromise` for any `GET /callback?code=…` with no check that the code belongs to this login, `github-auth.guard.ts:24` no longer stores a nonce, and `auth.controller.ts:127` no longer echoes one back. The CLI then exchanges that code at `/auth/cli/exchange` and `saveSession()` (login.ts:138) persists whatever account it maps to, overwriting the user's session. The port is guessable and any page in the user's browser can navigate to it (RFC 8252 §8.9), so the terminal can be silently pointed at another account's session. The deleted `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` was the only regression guard. Primary ownership is the security lens; raised here because the outcome is a wrong/overwritten persisted session (state corruption), and because the delta also removes the only test of that behaviour.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. login.ts:168-182 accepts any GET /callback with a non-empty `code` param and resolves the login promise at :223-226 with no state/nonce/CSRF binding to the flow this process started; the OAuth URL built at login.ts:36 sends only `mode` and `port`, so no client-side nonce ever exists. github-auth.guard.ts:24 destructures only `stateToken` from `createState()` and throws away the `csrf` that cli-auth.store.ts:25 generates, and auth.controller.ts:127-129 redirects with `?code=` only, never echoing `state.csrf` returned by consumeState() (cli-auth.store.ts:46). The backend state token guards only the browser->backend leg (port binding, expiry, BadRequestException at auth.controller.ts:134); nothing guards the browser->CLI leg. The unvalidated code is then exchanged (login.ts:56-60) and saveSession() at login.ts:138 unconditionally overwrites the persisted session with whatever account cliExchange resolves (auth.controller.ts:150-161). No test in packages/cli/test/ covers this handler. Cannot refute on not-present (code present), already-guarded (no guard on the loopback leg found), or counterexample. Although the primary lens is security, the concrete outcome — external input silently overwriting the persisted session with another account's tokens — is a data-overwrite/state-corruption defect within the correctness lane, so out-of-scope is not a sufficient ground to drop it.

mergedFrom.summary: CLI login now hard-fails (30s hang, then a misleading "Login timed out") whenever the backend does not echo `state`

finding.summary: CLI unconditionally requires a `state` echo the backend may not send — login then hangs 30s and fails with an unrelated timeout message
finding.evidence: login.ts:206 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, but the backend only appends it conditionally: `const stateEcho = state.nonce ? \`&state=…\` : ''` (auth.controller.ts:130). `state.nonce` is undefined whenever GitHubAuthGuard dropped it — non-string (duplicate `?nonce=a&nonce=b` makes express give an array), empty, or >128 chars (github-auth.guard.ts:34-38) — and, more importantly, whenever the CLI runs against a deployed backend that predates this change. In all those cases the genuine callback is answered with HTTP 400 'Invalid state', the promise never settles, and the user waits the full 30s for 'Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.' — a message that gives no hint of the real cause. There is no negotiation, version check, or diagnostic for the nonce-absent case.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed mechanism is absent from the working tree. (1) The CLI callback handler in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-227 reads only `code` (line 177) and never reads or validates a `state`/nonce param; the cited login.ts:206 is CSS (`box-shadow: ...`) inside the success HTML, not a state rejection, and the only 400 is `Missing code` (lines 178-182). The CLI also never sends a nonce — the OAuth URL at line 36 is `?mode=cli&port=${port}` only. (2) auth.controller.ts:127-129 redirects with `?code=${encodeURIComponent(code)}` and contains no `stateEcho` variable or conditional `&state=` append; line 130 is a closing brace. (3) github-auth.guard.ts is only 31 lines, so the cited lines 34-38 do not exist, and the guard performs only a port-range check (lines 21-26) with no nonce handling. (4) CliAuthStore's StateEntry is `{ csrf, mode, port, expiresAt }` (cli-auth.store.ts:4-9), so `state.nonce` cannot exist. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` yields only a design doc, a spellcheck dictionary, and the `get-nonce` npm package — nothing in the CLI or backend auth code. Because the CLI never inspects `state`, the described hang-then-30s-timeout path is not reachable by this mechanism.

mergedFrom.summary: backendErrorEnvelope silently discards non-`{error:{…}}` backend bodies, losing the server's message (Nest default error shape)

finding.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` discards the server's error message for bodies whose `error` is not an object (e.g. Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error: "Not Found"}`)
finding.evidence: `raw = data?.error`; when `raw` is a string (Nest's default exception body puts the reason phrase in `error` and the real text in `message`), the `typeof raw === 'object'` test at formatter.ts:101 fails, `fields` is `{}`, and the emitted envelope becomes `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`. The call sites still gate on truthiness of `error` (docs.ts:197, docs.ts:267, notes.ts:150/215, slides.ts:156/216), so this path is taken exactly where the old code printed the body verbatim and preserved `body.message` (including ValidationPipe's message array). Backend endpoints that are not hand-shaped (`{error:{code,message}}`) therefore lose their diagnostic text on `docs content`, `docs export`, `notes/slides content`, `files upload/download` and the import orchestrators.

verdict.reason: The claimed behavior does not exist. `backendErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:118-140) does have the `typeof raw === 'object'` test at line 126, and `fields` is `{}` for a string `error`, but the message is not taken from `fields` alone: lines 132-136 resolve it as `messageText(fields.message) ?? messageText(body?.message) ?? messageText(raw) ?? fallback.message`. For Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error: "Not Found"}` body the second link returns the server's `message`, and `messageText` (formatter.ts:91-99) explicitly joins a ValidationPipe `message[]` array rather than dropping it, falling back to the bare `error` string before ever reaching `HTTP <status>`. Tests output.test.ts:273-289, :291-304 and :306-315 assert exactly these three cases produce 'Document not found', 'title must be a string; title should not be empty' and 'Forbidden'. The cited call site docs.ts:195-211 gates on truthiness of `body?.error`, so a bare string `error` is truthy and does enter the function — where the message is preserved, not discarded. Therefore no diagnostic text is lost on the enumerated commands.
